correctness.rationale: Ball–Critcher's exact formula gives \(R_I\) as the positive root of \(x^2-a x-(r-a)=0\) with \(r=R_*\) and \(0<a\le r\). Evaluating at \(x=r\) and \(x=\sqrt r\) yields the stated sharp one-model envelope and endpoint equality. For two growing models, \(R_{I,A}>\sqrt{r_A}\) and \(R_{I,B}\le r_B\), so reversal is impossible at \(r_A\ge r_B^2\). Conversely, one-person households realize \(R_I=R_*=r_B\), while fixed-size households with local rate \(\lambda\to\infty\) have expected household outbreak size tending to the household size; choosing the global rate to keep \(R_*=r_A\) drives \(a\downarrow0\) and \(R_I\downarrow\sqrt{r_A}<r_B\). The exact four-person witness was independently checked from the displayed Markov recursion: \(m_4(2)=779/225\), \(R_*=3\), and \(p_3(2)=104/779>0\).
risks: The sharp lower endpoint is generally a limit rather than an attained value when the global contact rate must stay positive.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 article was read through the reproduction-number comparison theorem and proof. It supplies the exact quadratic and \(u^\top v=R_*-a\), and explicitly warns that \(R_*\) can be misleading across household structures, but it states only the standard within-model ordering. The square-root envelope is an elementary consequence of its identities, so that part alone is not treated as a large novelty claim. The surviving contribution is the exact cross-model reversal boundary together with the all-points sharpness construction and an exact finite witness. Resultary and the broader household-reproduction comparison literature located no theorem stating or implying the full quadratic frontier.
residual_risks: The 2016 comparison paper was not re-read in full during this execution, so an equivalent reformulation there remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The source itself emphasizes that \(R_*\) can mis-rank epidemics with different household structures. The theorem answers that concrete comparison problem sharply: it gives the exact universal no-reversal region and proves every point below the boundary is genuinely realizable by finite household models. That model-class classification is more informative than the routine one-model root inequalities.
risks: The theorem compares only \(R_*\) and \(R_I\); it does not order outbreak probability, final size, growth rate, or vaccination thresholds.
sources: assigned constructive sharpness proof and exact witness

limitations: The square-root endpoint is limiting in general.
